"""Category, subcategory and feature sales impact for the Impact tab.

The numbers come from ``app.analysis.chinese_pairs``: the market-adjusted China sales change
of version pairs that added a feature, minus that of pairs that did not, per year after launch.
News topics are attached to a subcategory as recent signals only: they get no sales effect of
their own.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from functools import cache
from pathlib import Path

from app.analysis.chinese_pairs import CATEGORIES, OUTPUT_DIR, SUBCATEGORIES, YEARS
from app.paths import ROOT_DIR

DEFAULT_IMPACT_FILE = OUTPUT_DIR / "impact.csv"
DEFAULT_NEWS_FILE = ROOT_DIR / "frontend" / "src" / "content" / "china_tech_trends.json"

# News topic ids (Feature Radar) per subcategory.
NEWS_BY_SUBCATEGORY = {
    "battery_range": ("solid_state", "sodium_ion"),
    "charging_replenishment": ("ultra_charging", "battery_swap", "v2g"),
    "high_voltage_powertrain": ("hv_800v",),
    "assisted_driving": ("urban_noa", "e2e_vla", "l3_autonomy"),
    "perception_compute": ("lidar", "adas_chips"),
    "autonomous_mobility": ("robotaxi",),
    "cockpit_intelligence": ("cockpit_llm",),
    "vehicle_compute": ("central_compute",),
    "software_lifecycle": ("ota",),
    "cross_device_ecosystem": ("phone_car_eco",),
    "seating_comfort": ("smart_seats",),
    "ride_body_control": ("active_suspension",),
    "by_wire_controls": ("steer_by_wire",),
    "body_manufacturing": ("giga_casting",),
    "lighting_visibility": ("smart_lighting",),
}


def _number(value: str) -> float | None:
    return float(value) if value not in ("", None) else None


def _series(row: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Impact points for the years that have an estimate."""
    return [
        {"year": year,
         "impact_pct": float(row[f"impact_pct_year_{year}"]),
         "lower_pct": float(row[f"lower_pct_year_{year}"]),
         "upper_pct": float(row[f"upper_pct_year_{year}"]),
         "pairs": int(float(row[f"n_with_year_{year}"]))}
        for year in YEARS if _number(row[f"impact_pct_year_{year}"]) is not None
    ]


def _load_news(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, dict]]:
    source = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    topics = {}
    for topic in source["topics"]:
        topics[topic["id"]] = {
            "id": topic["id"],
            "label": topic["label_en"],
            "label_cn": topic["label_cn"],
            "category": topic["bmw_domain"],
            "priority": topic.get("priority"),
            "signal": topic.get("signal"),
            "momentum_pct_change": topic.get("momentum_pct_change"),
            "volume_recent": topic.get("volume_recent", 0),
            "breadth_outlets": topic.get("breadth_outlets", 0),
            "headline": topic.get("headlines", [{}])[0].get("title", ""),
            "headline_url": topic.get("headlines", [{}])[0].get("link", ""),
        }
    return source, topics


def build_impact_taxonomy(impact_path: Path, news_path: Path) -> dict:
    with impact_path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as stream:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(stream))
    news_source, news_by_id = _load_news(news_path)
    unmapped = sorted(set(news_by_id) - {i for ids in NEWS_BY_SUBCATEGORY.values() for i in ids})
    if unmapped:
        raise ValueError(f"news topics without a subcategory: {unmapped}")

    by_level = {(row["level"], row["name"]): row for row in rows}
    features = [
        {"name": row["name"], "category": row["category"], "subcategory": row["subcategory"],
         "models": json.loads(row["models"]), "pair_count": int(row["pair_count"]), "impact_by_year": _series(row)}
        for row in rows if row["level"] == "feature"
    ]
    features = [f for f in features if f["impact_by_year"]]
    categories = []
    for category in CATEGORIES:
        subcategories = []
        for sub_id, (label, parent) in SUBCATEGORIES.items():
            if parent != category:
                continue
            row = by_level.get(("subcategory", sub_id))
            news = [news_by_id[i] for i in NEWS_BY_SUBCATEGORY.get(sub_id, ()) if i in news_by_id]
            if row is None and not news:
                continue
            subcategories.append({
                "id": sub_id,
                "label": label,
                "pair_count": int(row["pair_count"]) if row else 0,
                "impact_by_year": (_series(row) or None) if row else None,
                "legacy_features": sorted((f for f in features if f["subcategory"] == sub_id),
                                          key=lambda f: -f["pair_count"]),
                "news_features": news,
            })
        row = by_level.get(("category", category))
        series = _series(row) if row else []
        if series:
            categories.append({
                "id": category.lower().replace(" & ", "-").replace(" ", "-"),
                "label": category,
                "pair_count": int(row["pair_count"]),
                "impact_by_year": series,
                "subcategories": subcategories,
            })

    return {
        "title": "Sales Impact Forecast",
        "as_of": news_source["generated_at"],
        "horizon_years": list(YEARS),
        "categories": categories,
        "legacy_feature_count": len(features),
        "news_feature_count": len(news_by_id),
        "method": "market-adjusted China sales change after a version launch: pairs that added the item minus "
                  "pairs that did not, per year after launch, with a 95% interval",
        "status": "observational_sales_association",
        "caveat": "Observational association from Chinese version pairs, not a causal estimate. Later years rest on "
                  "fewer, older pairs. News signals are mapped for context and get no sales effect of their own.",
        "source_plot": "data/analysis/chinese_pairs/plots/impact_by_subcategory.pdf",
    }


@cache
def impact_taxonomy() -> dict:
    return build_impact_taxonomy(DEFAULT_IMPACT_FILE, DEFAULT_NEWS_FILE)

"""Category and subcategory sales-impact view for the Forecast tab.

The numeric scenarios come from the same Chinese-200 forecast artifact and
planning-prior model used by ``official_sales.plot_feature_forecast``.  News
topics are attached as recent signals only: they do not receive an invented
sales effect until a comparable legacy feature is available.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
from functools import cache
from pathlib import Path

from app.analysis.official_sales import CATEGORY_IMPACT_PRIORS, FORECAST_SATURATION, YEARS

DEFAULT_FORECAST_FILE = DATA_DIR / "analysis" / "chinese_200" / "feature_sales_impact_4_year_forecast.csv"

def _trajectory(prior: float) -> list[dict]:
    return [
        {"year": year, "impact_pct": round(prior * FORECAST_SATURATION[year], 3)}
        for year in YEARS
    ]


def _load_legacy(path: Path) -> dict[str, dict]:
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as stream:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(stream))
    output = {}
    for row in rows:
        name = row["display_name"]
        output[name] = {
            "name": name,
            "category": row["category"],
            "models": json.loads(row["models"]),
            "pair_count": int(row["pair_count"]),
            "impact_by_year": [
                {
                    "year": year,
                    "impact_pct": round(float(row[f"estimated_sales_impact_year_{year}_pct"]), 3),
                    "lower_pct": round(float(row[f"lower_year_{year}_pct"]), 3),
                    "upper_pct": round(float(row[f"upper_year_{year}_pct"]), 3),
                }
                for year in YEARS
            ],
        }
    return output


def _load_news(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, dict]]:
    source = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    topics = {}
    for topic in source["topics"]:
        topics[topic["id"]] = {
            "id": topic["id"],
            "label": topic["label_en"],
            "label_cn": topic["label_cn"],
            "category": topic["bmw_domain"],
            "priority": topic.get("priority"),
            "signal": topic.get("signal"),
            "momentum_pct_change": topic.get("momentum_pct_change"),
            "volume_recent": topic.get("volume_recent", 0),
            "breadth_outlets": topic.get("breadth_outlets", 0),
            "headline": topic.get("headlines", [{}])[0].get("title", ""),
            "headline_url": topic.get("headlines", [{}])[0].get("link", ""),
        }
    return source, topics


def _mean_legacy_trajectory(features: list[dict]) -> list[dict] | None:
    if not features:
        return None
    return [
        {
            "year": year,
            "impact_pct": round(sum(f["impact_by_year"][year - 1]["impact_pct"] for f in features) / len(features), 3),
            "lower_pct": round(sum(f["impact_by_year"][year - 1]["lower_pct"] for f in features) / len(features), 3),
            "upper_pct": round(sum(f["impact_by_year"][year - 1]["upper_pct"] for f in features) / len(features), 3),
        }
        for year in YEARS
    ]


def build_impact_taxonomy(forecast_path: Path, news_path: Path) -> dict:
    legacy_by_name = _load_legacy(forecast_path)
    news_source, news_by_id = _load_news(news_path)
    categories: dict[str, dict] = {}
    used_legacy: set[str] = set()
    used_news: set[str] = set()

    for definition in SUBCATEGORY_TAXONOMY:
        category = definition["category"]
        if category not in categories:
            prior = CATEGORY_IMPACT_PRIORS[category]
            categories[category] = {
                "id": category.lower().replace(" & ", "-").replace(" ", "-"),
                "label": category,
                "impact_by_year": _trajectory(prior),
                "subcategories": [],
            }
        legacy = [legacy_by_name[name] for name in definition["legacy"] if name in legacy_by_name]
        news = [news_by_id[item] for item in definition["news"] if item in news_by_id]
        used_legacy.update(item["name"] for item in legacy)
        used_news.update(item["id"] for item in news)
        categories[category]["subcategories"].append({
            "id": definition["id"],
            "label": definition["label"],
            "impact_by_year": _mean_legacy_trajectory(legacy),
            "legacy_features": legacy,
            "news_features": news,
        })

    missing_legacy = sorted(set(legacy_by_name) - used_legacy)
    missing_news = sorted(set(news_by_id) - used_news)
    if missing_legacy or missing_news:
        raise ValueError(
            "subcategory taxonomy is incomplete: "
            f"legacy={missing_legacy or 'none'}, news={missing_news or 'none'}"
        )

    return {
        "title": "Sales Impact Forecast",
        "as_of": news_source["generated_at"],
        "horizon_years": list(YEARS),
        "categories": list(categories.values()),
        "legacy_feature_count": len(legacy_by_name),
        "news_feature_count": len(news_by_id),
        "method": "category planning prior × adoption saturation; subcategory is the mean of mapped Chinese-200 feature scenarios",
        "status": "scenario_estimate_not_sales_fitted",
        "caveat": "Planning scenario, not a causal or sales-fitted prediction. Recent news signals are mapped for context and do not receive an independent sales effect.",
        "source_plot": "data/analysis/chinese/plots/feature_sales_impact_4_year_forecast.pdf",
    }


@cache
def impact_taxonomy() -> dict:
    return build_impact_taxonomy(DEFAULT_FORECAST_FILE, DEFAULT_NEWS_FILE)

```

Analyze consecutive versions and feature/sales associations after the CSV has official sales values:

```bash
uv run python -m app.analysis.official_sales ../data/external/bmw_official_first_20.csv
```

This writes `data/analysis/version_sales_differences.csv` (year 1-4 absolute and percentage differences
versus the previous version), `feature_sales_associations.csv` (mean/median differences and positive-share
by newly added feature), a JSON summary, and PNG/PDF plots in `data/analysis/plots/`. Add an integer
`version_order` column when release dates alone
do not define the intended sequence. Feature results are observational associations, not proof of causation.

For the Chinese-OEM cohort, grab 20 explicit predecessor/successor pairs (40 rows) from official NIO and
Li Auto releases, then analyze them:

```bash
uv run python -m app.grabbers.chinese_official_pairs
uv run python -m app.analysis.official_sales ../data/external/chinese_official_20_pairs.csv \
  --output-dir ../data/analysis/chinese
```

The editable pair manifest is `backend/chinese_model_pair_seeds.csv`. `pair_id` keeps overlapping update
chains separate. NIO pages are fetched live. Li Auto's investor-relations host can reject non-browser HTTP
clients, so the grabber falls back to short, checked evidence from those same official pages and marks the
affected rows as `curated_official_page_fallback`. Official launch releases rarely disclose version-level
annual cumulative sales, so those fields remain blank until an official delivery export is joined.

When sales are unavailable, the analysis also writes `feature_catalog_by_category.csv`,
`feature_sales_impact_4_year_forecast.csv`, and a four-year scenario plot. Feature wording is standardized
into general archetypes and aggregated across all model pairs. The forecast is a market-wide planning
estimate, not a sales-fitted or causal model. It uses editable category priors, a feature multiplier, a
50%/72%/88%/100% adoption-saturation curve over years 1-4, and 35%-60% uncertainty based on independent-pair
coverage. When real version-level sales are added, use the observational association outputs above instead
of treating the scenario priors as measured impact.

Generate the interactive Plotly view for the current 200-pair candidate file:

```bash
uv run python -m app.analysis.interactive_feature_plot
```

The result is `data/analysis/chinese_200/plots/interactive_feature_impact.html`. It stacks category and
feature trajectories with years 1-4 on the x-axis and cumulative-sales improvement on the y-axis. Category
and feature buttons independently control visibility; every line includes its uncertainty band. A third,
separate figure uses `data/internal/sales_volumes.xlsx` to estimate BMW sales for 2030-2033. Choose a model,
market, and multiple features; the baseline extends the selected history's 2025-2030 CAGR and the feature
scenario applies the same additive impact rates and uncertainty ranges used in the feature plot.

**EV/PHEV market table** (`top_500_ev_phev_europe*.csv`, `;`-separated). BMW rows that are our vehicles become the vehicle's own
external facts: G60 = 5er/i5 Limousine (the Touring is G61, so it is excluded), G70 = 7er/i7. Non-BMW-Group rows in the same segment
become competitors: F70 → C-segment, G60 → E, G70 → F. Feature phrases are kept, except those that only restate a spec column.

**JSONL contract**: `data/external/*.jsonl`, one record per line:

+  sales year is complete are used.
+- `features.csv`: what the current version added (`pair_id, detail, feature, subcategory, category,
+  evidence, source_url`). `detail` is the OEM's own wording (e.g. "Shenxing 4C LFP battery"), `feature`
+  the shared name used across brands (e.g. "4C+ fast-charging battery"), `subcategory` an id from
+  `SUBCATEGORIES` in `app/analysis/chinese_pairs.py`, and `category` one of the 8 technology domains.
+- `model_sales.csv`: annual China sales per nameplate (`car_model, year, units, metric, source, url`), one
+- `market_sales.csv`: CPCA annual passenger-car retail, total and NEV, for the market adjustment.

+`impact.csv` (per feature, subcategory and category: mean market-adjusted change of pairs that added it
+minus pairs that did not, per year, with a 95% interval and n) and `plots/impact_by_subcategory.pdf`.
+Year 1 is the launch year for a January-March launch, otherwise the next calendar year; the baseline is
+the year before the launch year. An item needs 3 pairs with sales in a year to get an estimate. The
+results are observational associations, not causal effects. To extend the sample, add the next older
+pairs (and their features and sales) to the CSVs and rerun. Newer pairs can be added once their first

input.command:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-shengyin-Desktop-2026-10-10-EHL-code-Open-Trend-Tracker/3fd7f23b-806c-42e4-a247-3d41a3610973/scratchpad/cn && cat > select.py <<'EOF'
"""Curate candidates: one sales line per nameplate, drop unclean baselines, merge same-year updates, take newest N."""
import json, sys, collections
N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 100
rows = json.load(open("all_candidates.json"))
LINE = {"BYD Han EV": "BYD Han", "BYD Han DM": "BYD Han", "BYD Qin Plus DM-i": "BYD Qin Plus", "BYD Qin Plus EV": "BYD Qin Plus",
        "BYD Song Plus DM-i": "BYD Song Plus", "BYD Song Plus EV": "BYD Song Plus", "BYD Tang DM": "BYD Tang",
        "BYD Song Pro DM-i": "BYD Song Pro", "Exeed TXL (Lingyun)": "Exeed TXL", "Exeed RX (Yaoguang)": "Exeed Yaoguang",
        "Chery Little Ant (eQ1)": "Chery Little Ant", "Neta X (formerly Neta U)": "Neta X"}
DROP = {  # renamed lines, sub-lines, or a baseline year in which the nameplate was not on sale all year
    "BYD Seal 05 DM-i (ex-Destroyer 05)", "BYD Seal 07 DM-i (ex-Seal DM-i)", "BYD Seal", "BYD Qin L DM-i",
    "BYD Seal 06 DM-i", "BYD Sealion 07 EV", "BYD Song L DM-i", "BYD Yuan Up", "NIO ET5T", "Neta X",
    "Neta AYA (formerly Neta V)", "Geely Boyue"}
DROP_ROWS = {("Chery Tiggo 5x", "2024-12"), ("Chery Tiggo 7", "2024-11-01")}
def first_year(d): return int(d[:4]) if int(d[5:7] or 1) <= 3 else int(d[:4]) + 1
kept = []
for r in rows:
    r["car_model"] = LINE.get(r["car_model"], r["car_model"])
    if r["car_model"] in DROP or (r["car_model"], r["current_launch"]) in DROP_ROWS:
        continue
    if len(r["current_launch"]) == 7: r["current_launch"] += "-15"
    kept.append(r)
groups = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in kept: groups[(r["car_model"], first_year(r["current_launch"]))].append(r)
pairs = []
for (model, y1), g in groups.items():
    g.sort(key=lambda r: r["current_launch"])
    pairs.append({"car_model": model, "brand": g[0]["brand"], "powertrain": g[0]["powertrain"],
                  "change_type": max((r["change_type"] for r in g), key=["model_year_update", "facelift", "new_generation"].index),
                  "previous_version": g[0]["previous_version"], "previous_launch": str(g[0].get("previous_launch") or ""),
                  "current_version": " + ".join(dict.fromkeys(r["current_version"] for r in g)),
                  "current_launch": g[0]["current_launch"], "latest_launch": g[-1]["current_launch"],
                  "headline_new_features": [f for r in g for f in r["headline_new_features"]],
                  "source_url": " ".join(dict.fromkeys(r["source_url"] for r in g)), "merged": len(g)})
pairs.sort(key=lambda p: (p["latest_launch"], p["car_model"]), reverse=True)
sel = pairs[:N]
for i, p in enumerate(sel, 1):

  "Air suspension", "Adaptive dampers (CDC)", "Rear-wheel steering", "AWD / dual motor", "New engine / more power",

For every nameplate and every listed calendar year, find units sold IN CHINA (domestic; exclude exports) for the whole nameplate line (all powertrains combined, e.g. "BYD Han" = Han EV + Han DM; "BYD Qin Plus" = DM-i + EV; "BYD Song Plus" = DM-i + EV).
Rules:
- Use ONE consistent source series per nameplate across its years. Best: the "Sales" table on the model's English Wikipedia page (it usually cites CPCA retail, Yiche or Dongchedi insurance registrations) — fetch https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<Model_page> directly. Alternatives: CnEVPost / CarNewsChina annual model rankings, OEM annual reports, Chinese Wikipedia (zh.wikipedia.org) sales tables, carsalesbase.com, chinamobil.ru.
- Note the metric: "retail" (CPCA), "insurance_registrations", "wholesale", or "unspecified". If a series mixes China + export, say so in note, or use another series.
- Also give the nameplate's first China market launch (YYYY-MM) — the first ever version of this line, not the latest update.
- Never invent or interpolate numbers. If a year is not found, omit that row and list it as missing. The year 2026 is NOT needed.

for row in read_csv(input_dir / "model_sales.csv"):
        sales[row["car_model"]][int(row["year"])] = int(row["units"])
    market = {int(r["year"]): {"NEV": int(r["nev_retail"]), "ICE": int(r["total_retail"]) - int(r["nev_retail"])}
              for r in read_csv(input_dir / "market_sales.csv")}
    return pairs, features, sales, market


def pair_sales(pairs: list[dict], sales: dict, market: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Baseline and year 1-4 sales of each pair, raw and market-adjusted."""
    last_year = max(market)
    launches = defaultdict(list)
    for p in pairs:
        launches[p["car_model"]].append(p["current_launch"])
    rows = []
    for p in pairs:
        model, segment = p["car_model"], p["powertrain"]
        first = first_sales_year(p["current_launch"])
        base_year = int(p["current_launch"][:4]) - 1
        later = sorted(d for d in launches[model] if d > p["current_launch"])
        base = sales[model].get(base_year)
        row = {"pair_id": p["pair_id"], "brand": p["brand"], "car_model": model, "powertrain": segment,
               "change_type": p["change_type"], "current_version": p["current_version"],
               "current_launch": p["current_launch"], "successor_launch": later[0] if later else "",
               "baseline_year": base_year, "baseline_sales": base}
        for k in YEARS:
            year = first + k - 1
            units = sales[model].get(year) if year <= last_year else None
            change = excess = None
            if units and base:
                change = units / base - 1
                excess = math.log(units / base) - math.log(market[year][segment] / market[base_year][segment])
            row[f"year_{k}"] = year
            row[f"sales_year_{k}"] = units
            row[f"change_pct_year_{k}"] = None if change is None else round(change * 100, 2)
            row[f"excess_log_year_{k}"] = None if excess is None else round(excess, 4)
            row[f"status_year_{k}"] = ("not_yet_observable" if year > last_year else
                                       "missing_sales" if excess is None else "observed")
        rows.append(row)
    return rows

"""Compose Chinese feature evidence, BMW comments, sales trends, and PM overrides."""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from app.paths import INTERNAL_DIR, RUNTIME_DIR
from app.services.forecast import forecast_catalog

FEATURE_PATTERNS = {
    "900V system + 102 kWh battery": (r"\b(?:800|900)\s*v\b", r"high[- ]voltage", r"battery", r"electric range"),
    "Charging + battery-swap station network": (r"charg", r"wallbox", r"charging station", r"charging network", r"charging cable"),
    "World-model ADAS + point-to-point navigation": (r"driving assist", r"highway assist", r"adaptive cruise", r"lane ", r"parking assist", r"navigation"),
    "5 nm automotive SoC + full-domain E/E architecture": (r"operating system", r"connecteddrive", r"software", r"touchscreen", r"cockpit", r"display", r"voice control"),
    "CDC dampers + hydraulic rear-subframe bushings": (r"suspension", r"damper", r"damping", r"shock absorber", r"ride comfort"),
    "Software-controlled active chassis system": (r"chassis", r"driving dynamics", r"handling", r"active steering", r"active roll"),
    "Dual cushion airbags + seat-integrated belts": (r"airbag", r"seat ?belt", r"safety belt", r"restraint"),
    "Integrated cabin display + audio entertainment": (r"rear.?seat entertainment", r"theatre screen", r"display", r"infotainment", r"sound system", r"audio"),
    "Roof center speaker + Dirac RRM audio": (r"speaker", r"sound system", r"bowers", r"surround sound", r"audio"),
    "Second-row zero-gravity seats + leg support": (r"seat comfort", r"reclin", r"lounge seat", r"leg support", r"comfortable seat"),
    "Six-/seven-seat cabin configuration": (r"six[- ]seat", r"seven[- ]seat", r"third row", r"seating capacity"),
    "ADB matrix headlights + Double-Dash DRL": (r"headlight", r"high.?beam", r"exterior light", r"daytime.?running"),
    "New Moon Silver paint + 21-inch wheels": (r"paint", r"exterior colou?r", r"wheel", r"rim", r"tyre", r"tire"),
}
OVERRIDES_FILE = RUNTIME_DIR / "decision-dashboard-overrides.json"


def _sentiment(feedback_type: str) -> str:
    value = feedback_type.strip().casefold()
    if value == "likes":
        return "positive"
    if value in {"wants", "difficult to use", "defect"}:
        return "negative"
    return "neutral"


def _internal_comments(vehicle: str) -> list[dict]:
    path = INTERNAL_DIR / f"{vehicle}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx"
    if not path.exists():
        return []
    frame = pd.read_excel(path).fillna("")
    frame = frame.drop_duplicates(subset=["ID", "Customer Feedback", "Feedback Type"])
    return [{
        "id": str(row["ID"]),
        "text": str(row["Customer Feedback"]),
        "sentiment": _sentiment(str(row["Feedback Type"])),
        "source": path.name,
    } for row in frame.to_dict("records") if str(row["Customer Feedback"]).strip()]


def _uploaded_comments(document_id: str) -> list[dict]:
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{16}", document_id):
        raise ValueError("document_id must be the 16-character ID returned by customer-input processing")
    path = RUNTIME_DIR / "customer-input" / document_id / "result.json"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"unknown processed document {document_id}")
    if feature not in catalog_names:
        raise KeyError(f"unknown Chinese-derived feature {feature!r}")
    overrides = _read_overrides()
    key = f"{vehicle}:{feature}"
    allowed = {"display_name", "selected", "priority", "engineering_status", "note"}
    overrides[key] = {name: value for name, value in values.items() if name in allowed and value is not None}
    OVERRIDES_FILE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OVERRIDES_FILE.write_text(json.dumps(overrides, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return overrides[key]

def family(text):
    t = text.lower()
    for key, name in (("dongchedi", "dongchedi_registrations"), ("gasgoo", "gasgoo"), ("chinamobil", "yiche"),

    return "unknown"

    """Source series of one year's number; batch-1 labels list per-year sources like 'Gasgoo 2022-24, Yiche 2025'."""
    src, year = row["source"], int(row["year"])
    for name, a, b in re.findall(r"([A-Za-z.]+)\s+(20\d\d)(?:-(\d\d))?", src):
        if int(a) <= year <= (2000 + int(b) if b else int(a)):

pairs = read_csv(input_dir / "pairs.csv")
    features = read_csv(input_dir / "features.csv")
    ids = [p["pair_id"] for p in pairs]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("duplicate pair_id in pairs.csv")
    for f in features:
        if f["pair_id"] not in ids:
            raise ValueError(f"feature for unknown pair {f['pair_id']}: {f['detail']}")
        if f["subcategory"] not in SUBCATEGORIES:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown subcategory {f['subcategory']!r} for {f['detail']}")
        if SUBCATEGORIES[f["subcategory"]][1] != f["category"]:
            raise ValueError(f"{f['subcategory']} belongs to {SUBCATEGORIES[f['subcategory']][1]}, not {f['category']}")
    sales: dict[str, dict[int, tuple[int, str]]] = defaultdict(dict)
    for row in read_csv(input_dir / "model_sales.csv"):
        sales[row["car_model"]][int(row["year"])] = (int(row["units"]), row["series"])
    market = {int(r["year"]): {"NEV": int(r["nev_retail"]), "ICE": int(r["total_retail"]) - int(r["nev_retail"])}
              for r in read_csv(input_dir / "market_sales.csv")}
    return pairs, features, sales, market


def pair_sales(pairs: list[dict], sales: dict, market: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """Baseline and year 1-4 sales of each pair, raw and market-adjusted."""
    last_year = max(market)
    launches = defaultdict(list)
    for p in pairs:
        launches[p["car_model"]].append(p["current_launch"])
    rows = []
    for p in pairs:
        model, segment = p["car_model"], p["powertrain"]
        first = first_sales_year(p["current_launch"])
        base_year = int(p["current_launch"][:4]) - 1
        later = sorted(d for d in launches[model] if d > p["current_launch"])
        # a nameplate first sold after February of the baseline year has no full baseline year
        partial = p["nameplate_launch"][:7] > f"{base_year}-02"
        base, base_series = (None, "") if partial else sales[model].get(base_year, (None, ""))
        row = {"pair_id": p["pair_id"], "brand": p["brand"], "car_model": model, "powertrain": segment,
               "change_type": p["change_type"], "current_version": p["current_version"],
               "current_launch": p["current_launch"], "successor_launch": later[0] if later else "",
               "nameplate_launch": p["nameplate_launch"], "baseline_year": base_year, "baseline_sales": base}
        for k in YEARS:
            year = first + k - 1
            units, series = sales[model].get(year, (None, "")) if year <= last_year else (None, "")
            # a change between two different source series (e.g. wholesale vs registrations) is not a sales change
            broken = bool(units and base) and series != base_series
            change = excess = None
            if units and base and not broken:
                change = units / base - 1
                excess = math.log(units / base) - math.log(market[year][segment] / market[base_year][segment])
            row[f"year_{k}"] = year
            row[f"sales_year_{k}"] = units
            row[f"change_pct_year_{k}"] = None if change is None else round(change * 100, 2)
            row[f"excess_log_year_{k}"] = None if excess is None else round(excess, 4)
            row[f"status_year_{k}"] = ("not_yet_observable" if year > last_year else
                                       "partial_baseline" if partial else
                                       "series_break" if broken else
                                       "missing_sales" if excess is None else "observed")
        rows.append(row)
    return rows

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

# EV / hybrid version-pair search rules

Find *version transitions* of Chinese-brand passenger-car nameplates whose China sales are mainly
battery-electric (BEV), plug-in hybrid (PHEV/DM-i/EM-i/C-DM/iDD/Hi4) or range-extender (EREV).
Skip petrol lines, including petrol lines that merely added a hybrid variant (e.g. Haval H6 PHEV, Tiggo 9 C-DM).

Window: NEW version launched in China between 2021-01-01 and 2025-03-31. Work newest first, year by year,
and be exhaustive for each year before going to the older one.

A transition = previous version -> current version of the SAME nameplate (same line in China sales tables):
new generation, facelift, or model-year update that ADDS at least one concrete technical/equipment feature
(battery/range, charging speed, hybrid system generation, ADAS/NOA, LiDAR, cockpit chip/screens, suspension, seats...).
Skip: brand-new nameplates, price-cut/colour/trim-only editions, export-only, renamed lines.

Eligibility (check both, they decide whether the sales data can be used):
- the nameplate (its first-ever version) went on sale in China no later than February of the calendar year
  BEFORE the new version's launch year (so that baseline year is a full sales year);
- it sold roughly >= 10,000 units in China in that baseline year.

Already known transitions are listed in known_transitions.txt in the same folder — do NOT repeat them
(different launch dates of the same nameplate are fine).

Per transition give: brand, car_model (English nameplate as in China sales rankings, all powertrains of the
line combined, e.g. "BYD Han"), powertrain "NEV", change_type ("new_generation"|"facelift"|"model_year_update"),
nameplate_first_launch (YYYY-MM), previous_version, previous_launch, current_version, current_launch
(official China launch, YYYY-MM-DD preferred), headline_new_features (2-5 strings), source_url (official OEM
newsroom, CnEVPost, CarNewsChina, Autohome, IT之家, Wikipedia; Gasgoo blocks fetching), baseline_sales_estimate.

The web-search budget is shared with other agents: use at most 55 WebSearch calls. Prefer WebFetch of known
pages (Wikipedia model pages list versions and dates; CnEVPost tag pages). Never invent; verify dates.
EOF
echo ok
